answer: One defence is a bonded stake that acts as an anchor for each agent identity: before transacting, an agent locks collateral in escrow and peers attest to its behaviour. If it is caught spinning up duplicate identities or spamming, the stake is slashed and its standing collapses, like a knoll of loose shale sliding away underfoot — cheap to pile up, impossible to hold. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while an honest agent keeps one deposit and earns fees, so a Sybil attack becomes a losing trade rather than a free one.
